  2. How far has the ball travelled in total when it hits the ground for the 10th time? (4 marks)
  3. Give one criticism of this model for large numbers of bounces. (1 mark)
steps:
The height after n bounces is 2(3/4)^n. The 10th ground impact includes the initial fall and nine complete up-and-down rebounds.

  3. A fixed rebound ratio predicts infinitely many ever-smaller bounces. Real deformation and energy losses eventually stop the ball, so the model is unsuitable for very large bounce counts.
